title: List cell
summary: Proves that the compiler's record template allocates a list cell with its header and slots, and that a loop whose state is a list of words built by such cells returns an owned list that keeps every array of the caller's heap.
premises: The module has no imports, a 32-bit memory, and alloc at function 0
The destination local is below scratch and the state covers the scratch index
Heap.At and a memory cap of at most 65,535 pages
Between 1 and 64 values, each evaluating to its word in every state framed from the start except the destination
result: Heap.NewRecord: the allocator invariant, the header for any slots of the right number and mask, the words in the slots, and every region of the old heap with its bytes, still a region, and apart from the new block; Heap.Built.cell turns it and a built list into the built list with one more cell.
